extracted.intended_audience: independent inventors, small businesses, and pro se patent applicants (especially low‑income applicants in CO, MT, NM, UT, WY) seeking free legal assistance for patents and trademarks
extracted.subtask_description: A university library research guide listing local, regional, and national pro bono and low‑cost patent/trademark legal resources, eligibility rules, availability constraints, and contact points for inventor support. Includes USPTO pro se resources and law clinic information.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProBoPat eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants are residents of Colorado, Montana, New Mexico, Utah, or Wyoming who have an annual income of three times the federal poverty guidelines or less and who, in ProBoPat’s sole discretion, would benefit from the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ProBoPat connects low‑income inventors with patent practitioners for patent preparation and prosecution legal services on a pro bono (free) basis and provides access to business consulting and training for bringing new ideas to market. Eligibility is geographic, income‑based, and subject to program discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProBoPat services (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ProBoPat program connects low-income inventors with patent practitioners for patent preparation and prosecution legal services on a pro bono (free) basis as well as provides access to business consulting and training for bringing new ideas to market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services include patent preparation and prosecution and business consulting/training to help bring ideas to market; applicants should expect the program to focus on inventors who both meet eligibility and are judged likely to benefit from assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: BYU Law & Entrepreneurship Clinic (LEC) availability and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law & Entrepreneurship Clinic (LEC) at BYU Laws accepts applications on an on going, rolling basis. While we hope that we can assist you, our resources are limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEC is only staffed and available to assist entrepreneurs from late August through mid April. If you have pressing legal needs, do not wait for LEC assistance and seek other legal assistance (the clinic can provide referrals).

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Patent Pro Bono Program scope and matching
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's website shows the nationwide network of independently operated regional programs that match volunteer patent professionals with financially under-resourced inventors and small businesses for the purpose of securing patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The network is nationwide but regionally/independently operated; eligibility generally targets financially under‑resourced inventors and small businesses—check the USPTO page or regional programs for specific requirements and application steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Law School Clinic Certification Program (clinic listing/scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO list of law school clinics that offer varying areas of intellectual property practice and geographical support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law school clinics differ in the IP areas they cover and the geographic regions they serve; consult the USPTO certification list to identify clinics that match your needs and location.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Pro Se Assistance Program policy and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pro Se Assistance Program provides outreach and education to applicants (also known as 'pro se' applicants) who file patent applications without the assistance of a registered patent attorney or agent. USPTO employees cannot give legal advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program aims to increase the quality of pro se applications and assist pro se applicants with making informed decisions regarding their patent applications. Expect outreach/education (not legal advice) and use the program to improve application quality and decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTRC resources and contact availability
rubrics_metrics.description: This guide features our Patent and Trademark Resource Center's (PTRC) resources and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTRC representatives (contact names, emails, and scheduling options are provided) can be contacted for assistance, virtual meetings, and referrals; the PTRC is a local point of contact for inventor resources and guidance but is distinct from providing legal advice.
